Premises: (1) the detector is intended to distinguish cross-model duplicate finding IDs from same-model duplicate finding IDs; (2) if `model_id` is absent on multiple colliding findings, all such findings are collapsed to the same `"?"` value; (3) `cross_model` is derived from `len(model_ids) > 1`. Concrete trace: two distinct finding objects `A` and `B` with `finding_id="F001"` and no `model_id` produce `model_ids=["?"]`, so `cross_model=False`, even though the detector lacks evidence that the duplicates came from the same model. This silently under-reports unknown-source collisions.
FOLLOW: The collision record feeds the module-level `_finding_id_collisions` accumulator and the warning log. Downstream post-mortem tooling uses `model_ids` and `cross_model` to quantify whether UUID namespacing is needed. If unknown model IDs collapse to `"?"`, multiple independent unknown sources are reported as one source, causing `cross_model=False`; that can bias the Exp 41 UUID-namespace go/no-go evidence toward “same-model duplicate only” when the available evidence does not justify that conclusion.
ANALYSE: HARD correctness constraint. Premises: `model_ids` is a set, set cardinality controls `cross_model`, and missing `model_id` currently maps all missing values to the same sentinel. Derivation: for inputs `[A, B]` where both have `finding_id="F001"` and neither has `model_id`, the set comprehension yields `{"?"}`; `len({"?"}) == 1`; therefore `cross_model` is false. The detector’s stated purpose is to observe collision provenance, so collapsing distinct unknown provenance objects is silently wrong. Status: CONFIRMED.
